meta.description: Designs and validates quantitative targeted metabolomics assays (MRM/SRM on triple-quadrupole, PRM on high-resolution instruments) to report absolute concentrations. Covers the internal-standard strategy (external cal -> global IS -> standard addition -> stable-isotope-labeled IS), weighted calibration judged by back-calculated %RE not R-squared, ion-ratio quantifier/qualifier confirmation, matrix-effect/recovery characterization, and ICH M10 method validation. Use when quantifying a closed panel of known metabolites with units, building or validating an LC-MS/MS assay, choosing an IS or calibration weighting, or judging whether a reported concentration is trustworthy.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 7 executed/generated outputs derive numbers from computed synthetic data (explicitly labelled synthetic); no fabricated DOI/PMID/statistics. The 7 cited references in SKILL.md are real, verifiable publications (unchanged by the fix).

practice_boundaries.detail: Scope remains bioanalytical assay validation and method development, not individual patient diagnosis or prescription; no diagnostic/prescriptive language in any of the 7 outputs.

methodological_ground.detail: The pre-fix audit's flagged methodological gap is now closed: SKILL.md's new 'Precision: Intra-Day and Inter-Day (Nested ANOVA, Not Pooled SD)' subsection is placed inline in the default workflow sequence (between LOD/LLOQ and Per-Method Failure Modes) and the Quantitative Thresholds table's precision row now points to it, so an agent following the Skill's normal read-order reaches the correct formula by default, not as an aside. Independently re-derived (Input 6, and a verbatim copy-paste of SKILL.md's own code block) and confirmed: naive pooled SD reads 18.9% (wrongly PASSes the 20% LLOQ tolerance) vs. nested ANOVA 21.1% (correctly FAILs) -- reproducing the fix log's numbers from first principles, not on trust.

code_usability.detail: All R code across 7 inputs ran to completion with base R only (no additional packages), no missing dependencies, no syntax errors, via F:/OpenScience/audit-envs/untargeted-metabolomics-analyst/rs.sh. SKILL.md's own new Precision code block was executed byte-for-byte (not paraphrased) and reproduced its inline comments exactly (21.7%/20.6% intra-day, 18.9% naive, 21.1% nested). The bundled examples/targeted_quantification.R (unchanged by the fix) still runs unmodified.

functional_suitability.note: Now covers calibration/weighting, IS normalization, ion-ratio, LOD/LLOQ, and -- new in this fix -- intra/inter-day precision with runnable nested-ANOVA code, plus a Report Format section. Matrix factor, recovery, and carryover are still documented only as threshold-table rows with a prose formula, not a runnable code block (down-scoped from a P1 to a P2 in this re-audit, since the highest-risk gap -- inter-day precision silently passing a failing assay -- is fixed and the remaining formulas are simple ratio/percentage arithmetic, not error-prone variance decompositions).

reliability.note: Unchanged from pre-fix: hard-stop/NA-below-LLOQ is correct defensive design; boolean pass/id_confirmed flags are structured. Still no documented handling for missing calibrator levels, non-monotonic curves, or negative back-calculated concentrations.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md grew 211 -> 269 lines (new Precision + Report Format sections); usage-guide.md shrank 74 -> 60 lines via the redundancy pass. Still compact, no redundant round-trips.

agent_usability.note: The pre-fix Feedback Design gap ('no explicit final-report/output-format template') is now closed by the new Report Format section (verified present and specific: sample x analyte table with a required non-blank reason for unreportable results). Learnability/Consistency/Error Prevention remain strong and were re-verified unchanged across regression Inputs 1-5.

human_usability.note: Unchanged: usage-guide.md's example prompts still aid discoverability post-redundancy-pass (verified all 5 Example Prompt bullets survive). recommendations.title: Matrix factor, recovery, and carryover still lack runnable code
recommendations.problem: The pre-fix P1 covered accuracy/precision/matrix-factor/carryover collectively; this fix added runnable code only for precision (correctly prioritized -- it was the one with a real silent-failure risk). Matrix factor and carryover are still threshold-table rows with a prose formula, not a code block.
recommendations.root_cause: The fix targeted the one formula an agent could get quantitatively wrong (nested variance components); matrix factor and carryover are simple ratio/percentage arithmetic an agent is unlikely to derive incorrectly, so they were left as documentation.
recommendations.fix: If time allows in a future pass, add a short code block for IS-normalized matrix factor and carryover-as-%-of-LLOQ, matching the style of the new Precision subsection, for full parity with the calibration/IS-normalization/ion-ratio sections.

recommendations.title: Description remains jargon-dense for non-expert trigger phrasing
recommendations.problem: The frontmatter description relies on MRM/SRM/ion-ratio/%RE vocabulary; a user phrasing a request without this vocabulary may under-trigger relative to sibling skills.
recommendations.root_cause: Description is written for an expert audience; this is an explicit, logged trade-off (fixes/bio-metabolomics-targeted-analysis.md), not an oversight -- the description already disambiguates against 3 sibling skills.
recommendations.fix: Optionally add one plain-language trigger phrase (e.g. 'give me a concentration in units for a known compound') alongside the technical terms; not required for deployment.
